summary: Mauritius has the best-documented African residence-by-investment routes: property purchase (USD 375,000 since 2020, earlier USD 500,000), investor occupation permits (USD 50,000-100,000), retiree permits and a 2021 USD 250,000 family permit, all traceable through Finance Acts and the Immigration Act 2022, plus a dormant reduced-residence naturalisation clause for investors (MUR 3 million in 1995, USD 500,000 from 1999); the only official counts are EDB stock figures for June 2021. Seychelles offers permanent residence for USD 1 million investors and an Eden Island residence permit, with no numbers. Sierra Leone's GO-FOR-GOLD citizenship has no published legal basis (only a press release and promoter claims), and Botswana's and Nigeria's plans are at bill stage; none gets a programme row.

sources.title: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 (Act No. 7 of 2020)
sources.publisher: Republic of Mauritius (Government Gazette No. 98 of 7 August 2020, Legal Supplement)

Third Schedule: new EDB Act First Schedule (investor USD 50,000; retiree USD 1,500 a month).
sources.notes: Copy hosted by the Mauritius Revenue Authority. The EDB Act consolidation notes this Act commenced on 7 Aug 2020 and 2 Sep 2020 for different provisions.

sources.title: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2021 (Act No. 15 of 2021)
sources.publisher: Republic of Mauritius (Government Gazette No. 121 of 5 August 2021, Legal Supplement)

sources.notes: Copy hosted by the Mauritius Revenue Authority. Parts of the text layer are mis-encoded (shifted characters); quotes are taken only from clean passages.

sources.title: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2023 (Act No. 12 of 2023)
sources.publisher: Republic of Mauritius (Government Gazette No. 62 of 20 July 2023, Legal Supplement)
sources.covers: s. 37: residence permit for buyers of senior-living PDS property above USD 200,000 aged over 50; Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act route for residents buying one property outside the schemes at USD 500,000 or more.
sources.notes: Copy hosted by the Mauritius Revenue Authority.

sources.title: The Finance Act 2025 (Act No. 18 of 2025)
sources.publisher: Republic of Mauritius (Government Gazette No. 66 of 9 August 2025, Legal Supplement)
sources.covers: s. 13: new EDB Act First Schedule (investor USD 50,000 or USD 100,000; retiree USD 2,000 a month; permanent residence after 5 years; Family Occupation Permit still USD 250,000). s. 25: Immigration Act 2022 sections 10-12 replaced (retiree permit 10 years; permanent residence 20 years).
sources.notes: Assented 8 Aug 2025. Copy hosted by the Mauritius Revenue Authority. Contradicts some industry summaries that said retiree and investor permits were cut to 5 years: the Act keeps 10 years.

sources.title: The Immigration Act 2022 (Act No. 14 of 2022)
sources.publisher: Republic of Mauritius (Government Gazette No. 106 of 27 July 2022, Legal Supplement)
sources.covers: Replaces the Immigration Act 1970. s. 8: residence permit for property buyers under IRS, RES, IHS, PDS or Smart City Scheme, or G+2 apartments, at USD 375,000; s. 10 retiree permit; s. 12 occupation permits.
sources.notes: Gazette copy as hosted by UNODC SHERLOC; not found on a Mauritian government site in this pass.

sources.title: Immigration Act (Act 13 of 1970), consolidated text
sources.publisher: Republic of Mauritius (consolidated text)
sources.covers: Consolidated text showing amendments up to 2009: resident status for IRS owners and RES owners at USD 500,000 (s. 5(1)(g)); occupation permit (s. 9A) and retiree permit (s. 9B) inserted with effect from 1 Oct 2006.
sources.notes: As hosted by UNODC SHERLOC; PDF created March 2011; last amendment listed is Act 1 of 2009. Unofficial consolidation.

sources.title: Economic Development Board Act (Act 11 of 2017), consolidated text as amended to Act 13 of 2026
sources.publisher: Economic Development Board, Mauritius
sources.covers: First Schedule as in force from 13 Aug 2026: investor occupation permit USD 100,000; retiree USD 2,000 a month; permanent residence criteria incl. golden visa holders investing USD 1 million; no Family Occupation Permit criteria.
sources.notes: Consolidation published by the EDB; amending Act 13 of 2026 itself was not obtained. 'Golden visa' is defined as a visa issued under the Passports Act on EDB recommendation; its own criteria were not found.

sources.title: The Mauritius Citizenship (Amendment) Act 1995 (Act No. 24 of 1995)
sources.publisher: Republic of Mauritius
sources.covers: s. 5: naturalisation after 2 years' residence (instead of 5 of 7) for a person who has invested at least MUR 3,000,000 in Mauritius.
sources.notes: Scanned copy (with the Constitution amendment) hosted by the Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative; text read by OCR, so quotes may contain OCR errors.

sources.title: The Mauritius Citizenship (Amendment) Act 1999 (Act No. 34 of 1999)
sources.publisher: Republic of Mauritius
sources.covers: Raises the investment for reduced-residence naturalisation from MUR 3,000,000 to USD 500,000 'or such other sum as may be prescribed'.
sources.notes: Copy from the GLOBALCIT database. Passed 30 Nov 1999; assent date printed partly illegibly ('7th December 1999', possibly the 17th). The Act's own short-title clause says '1998'.

sources.title: Mauritius Citizenship Act (RL 3/585), consolidated text
sources.publisher: Prime Minister's Office, Mauritius (consolidated text)
sources.covers: Consolidated s. 9 (naturalisation), incl. s. 9(3) reduced residence for investors.
sources.notes: PDF metadata: author 'pmo', created 26 May 2003. Its s. 9(3) reads '5,000 US dollars', which conflicts with the 1999 amending Act (USD 500,000) and is probably a transcription error in the consolidation. Annotations list amendments only up to 1995, so the consolidation may not include the 1999 Act properly. The current official text was not obtained.

observations.notes: Active occupation permits in the Investor category on 30 June 2021 (main permit holders only). Investors who hold residence through property schemes are not included. The same figure appears in an infographic on PDF p. 11.

Active residence permits of retired non-citizens (main holders) on 30 June 2021. The indicator is defined for investor-linked permits; here it counts retiree permits, which require income transfers rather than an investment.

observations.quote: there were 427 Permanent Resident Permit holders as of 30th June 2021
observations.notes: All categories of permanent residence permit (investors, professionals, self-employed, retirees); not split by category. New indicator proposed.

observations.quote: As of 30 June 2021, in addition to the main permit holders, there were 5138 dependents issued with a residence permit to live in Mauritius.
observations.notes: Dependants of all occupation-permit and retiree-permit holders, including professionals (employees), so not only investors' families. The source says 'dependents issued with a residence permit'; recorded as permits.

observations.location: PDF p. 11 (report p. 16-17), infographic 'Period of July 2020 to June 2021'
observations.quote: Authorisations issued for acquisition of residential property: 286 (Value : MUR 10.3 billion)
observations.notes: EDB authorisations for non-citizens to acquire residential property, July 2020 to June 2021 (the Mauritian fiscal year). Not all purchases necessarily qualified for a residence permit (only those of at least USD 375,000).

observations.location: PDF p. 11 (report p. 16-17), infographic 'Period of July 2020 to June 2021'
observations.quote: Authorisations issued for acquisition of residential property: 286 (Value : MUR 10.3 billion)
observations.notes: Value of the 286 residential acquisitions authorised by the EDB in FY2020/21. Covers all authorised purchases by non-citizens under EDB schemes, not only those that led to a residence permit; it is authorised value, not money received.

observations.location: p. 1, 'A Presidential Vision to Attract Foreign Direct Investment'
observations.quote: During its initial six-month product-market test, thirteen families received confirmation of naturalization under the President's prerogative
observations.notes: Claim by the GO-FOR-GOLD promoters, not confirmed by any government publication found. Counts families, not persons. The pilot period is not dated precisely (programme 'launched in January 2025'). No programme row exists because no law or regulation creating the route was found.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant and dependants (Real Estate Scheme buyer)
program_terms.location: s. 5(1)(g)(ii), PDF p. 3
program_terms.quote: under the Real Estate Scheme, the purchase price of which is not less than 500,000 US dollars or its equivalent in any other hard convertible foreign currency
program_terms.notes: Consolidated text with amendments to 1 Jan 2009; start date of the USD 500,000 rule not established. In this text owners under the Integrated Resort Scheme (s. 5(1)(g)(i)) had resident status with no price stated in the Act. valid_to is the date of the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2015, which rewrote s. 5(1)(g); whether RES/IRS kept a threshold between 2015 and 2020 is unclear (the 2015 Act kept existing IRS/RES residents' status).

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant and dependants (Property Development Scheme or Smart City Scheme buyer)
program_terms.location: s. 23(b)(i), new s. 5(1)(g) of the Immigration Act, PDF p. 57
program_terms.quote: he is a person who holds immovable property under the Property Development Scheme or Smart City Scheme, the purchase price of which is not less than 500,000 US dollars
program_terms.notes: Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2015, assented 14 May 2015. The Invest Hotel Scheme was added to the same paragraph by the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2017 (s. 25(a), in force July 2017).

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant and dependants (IRS, RES, IHS, PDS or Smart City Scheme buyer)
program_terms.location: s. 27(a)(i), new s. 5(1)(g) of the Immigration Act, PDF p. 55
program_terms.quote: Integrated Resort Scheme, Real Estate Scheme, Invest Hotel Scheme, Property Development Scheme or Smart City Scheme, the purchase price of which is not less than 375,000 US dollars
program_terms.notes: Act gazetted 7 Aug 2020 (some provisions from 2 Sep 2020). Carried into the Immigration Act 2022, s. 8(1)(d) and (e) (also allowing joint purchases where each buyer's share is at least USD 375,000). EDB guidelines (Nov 2024) and residency.mu still state USD 375,000 in 2026.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant and dependants (apartment in a building of at least ground plus 2 floors, outside the schemes)
program_terms.location: s. 37(b)(i), new s. 5(1)(ga) of the Immigration Act, PDF p. 120
program_terms.quote: provided the purchase price is not less than 375,000 US dollars or its equivalent in any other hard convertible foreign currency
program_terms.notes: 'G+2' route announced in Budget 2021/22. Carried into the Immigration Act 2022, s. 8(1)(f). Non-citizens may buy G+2 apartments from MUR 6 million, but only purchases of at least USD 375,000 give residence (residency.mu).

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant aged over 50 and dependants (senior-living property under the PDS)
program_terms.location: s. 37(b)(iii), new s. 8(1)(fa) of the Immigration Act 2022, PDF p. 66
program_terms.quote: he purchases or otherwise acquires a residential property under the Property Development Scheme related to senior living, provided that - (A) the purchase price exceeds 200,000 US dollars
program_terms.notes: Also requires the buyer to be aged above 50 at the time of application.

program_terms.applies_to: per application
program_terms.location: section 3.0, item 2, PDF p. 5
program_terms.quote: A non-refundable processing fee (per application submitted) of MUR 25,000 for acquisition in IRS/ RES/ PDS
program_terms.notes: EDB processing fee for property acquisition applications, as stated in the Nov 2024 guidelines; start date not known. Registration duty (5% or USD 70,000, whichever is lower, for first purchases in IRS/RES) is a tax and not recorded here.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (investor occupation permit)
program_terms.location: PDF p. 31 (report p. 56)
program_terms.quote: Initial investment requirement for Investor category was reviewed downwards from USD 100,000 to USD 50,000.
program_terms.notes: Earlier minimum for the investor occupation permit as described by the EDB; the date it was introduced was not established. Some variants existed (e.g. USD 100,000 partly in high-technology equipment, Finance Act 2017, item 1E).

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (investor occupation permit)
program_terms.location: Third Schedule, new First Schedule to the EDB Act, Part I item 1, PDF p. 168
program_terms.quote: Initial investment of USD 50,000 or its equivalent in freely convertible foreign currency
program_terms.notes: Permit valid 10 years from this Act (previously 3). Restated with turnover conditions in the Finance Act 2025 (Part I item 1). No longer in the EDB Act First Schedule as consolidated to Act 13 of 2026, so valid_to is that Act's commencement date (13 Aug 2026) as given in the consolidation.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (investor occupation permit)
program_terms.location: s. 13(d), new First Schedule to the EDB Act, Part I item 2, PDF p. 45
program_terms.quote: Initial investment of USD 100,000 or its equivalent in freely convertible foreign currency
program_terms.notes: Introduced alongside the USD 50,000 option (with lower turnover targets). From 13 Aug 2026 the only investor option in the EDB Act First Schedule (consolidation, Part I item 1: USD 100,000; turnover MUR 5 million from year 3; MUR 8 million for renewal from year 5).

program_terms.applies_to: investor seeking a permanent residence permit directly
program_terms.location: s. 27(b)(i), amending s. 5A(1)(aa) of the Immigration Act, PDF p. 55
program_terms.quote: in subsection (1)(aa), by deleting the words "500,000 US dollars" and replacing them by the words "375,000 US dollars"
program_terms.notes: Direct route to permanent residence for a qualifying investment; start date of the USD 500,000 level not established.

program_terms.applies_to: investor seeking a 20-year permanent residence permit directly
program_terms.location: Third Schedule, Part II item 1, PDF p. 172
program_terms.quote: Minimum investment of USD 375,000 in a qualifying business activity
program_terms.notes: The EDB describes this as 'The minimum investment amount for an investor to obtain a 20-Year Permanent Residence Permit was reduced from USD 500,000 to USD 375,000' (Annual Report 2020/21, p. 56). Repeated in the Finance Act 2021 schedule. The Finance Act 2025 schedule (Part IV) no longer contains it: permanent residence then requires 5 years on an investor occupation permit and turnover of MUR 15 million a year or MUR 75 million over 5 years.

program_terms.applies_to: golden visa holder seeking a permanent residence permit
program_terms.location: First Schedule, Part IV item 5, PDF p. 58
program_terms.quote: has invested an aggregate amount of not less than USD one million or its equivalent in any other freely convertible currency within a period of 12 months from the date of issuance of the golden visa, in any business activity other than acquisition of a residential property under the EDB property schemes
program_terms.notes: From the EDB's consolidation as amended to Act 13 of 2026 (commenced 13 Aug 2026 per the consolidation). The golden visa itself is issued under the Passports Act on EDB recommendation; its own criteria were not found.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant, on approval
program_terms.location: 'Key Features' box
program_terms.quote: Applicable fee USD 1,000 upon approval of application *New fees as from 11 July 2022
program_terms.notes: Permit fee payable to government on approval, per EDB residency portal (2026). The site also says the EDB charges no processing fee.

program_terms.applies_to: per application (occupation permit and retiree permit)

program_terms.location: 'Key Features' box
program_terms.quote: Applicable fee USD 1,000 *New fees as from 11 July 2022

Repeated unchanged in the Finance Act 2025 schedule. valid_to: the criteria no longer appear in the EDB's consolidation as amended to Act 13 of 2026; the permit itself is still defined in the Immigration Act 2022 text obtained, so treat the end as uncertain.

program_terms.location: s. 5, new s. 9(3) of the Mauritius Citizenship Act, PDF p. 2
program_terms.quote: where a person has invested in Mauritius a sum of not less than 3,000,000 rupees
program_terms.notes: Allows the Minister to accept 2 years' continuous residence instead of the normal residence requirement (12 months immediately before plus 5 of the previous 7 years). Text read by OCR. Discretionary; renunciation of other nationality was required by s. 9(4) of the consolidated text.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant
program_terms.location: s. 3, PDF p. 1
program_terms.quote: deleting the words "3,000,000 rupees" and replacing them by the words "500,000 US dollars or such other sum as may be prescribed"
program_terms.notes: Passed 30 Nov 1999, assented December 1999. A 2003 PMO consolidation prints '5,000 US dollars', apparently an error. Whether the provision is still in force, and whether a different sum was ever prescribed, was not established.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant
program_terms.location: 'Permanent Residence - Investors', p. 3
program_terms.quote: Type 1 Has invested 1,000,000 US Dollars or more in a business in Seychelles and has resided for 1 year in Seychelles
program_terms.notes: Type 2: same investment and at least 5 years of business association. Rules introduced by 2013 amendments to the Citizenship Act and Immigration Decree; exact commencement date not found. The 2013 application form says the investment is counted as 'an equivalent in Seychelles Rupees'.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant
program_terms.location: 'Investors', p. 1
program_terms.quote: Permit Fee: Sr. 150,000/-
program_terms.notes: Same amount in the 2020 fee list ('Investors: SCR 150,000'). Plus a SR 1,000 processing fee.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant
program_terms.location: 'Citizenship - Investor', p. 5
program_terms.quote: Has invested 1,000,000 US Dollars or more in a business in Seychelles and has resided for 11 years aggregate in Seychelles
program_terms.notes: Also requires 80% in a citizenship exam in a national language, three sponsors and newspaper and Gazette notices (Form IMM2). Not a quick citizenship-by-investment route.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant
program_terms.location: 'Special Circumstances', p. 1
program_terms.quote: Investors: SCR 350,000
program_terms.notes: Fee for citizenship under special circumstances, investor category, in the fee list published in 2020; start date not known.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant incl. spouse and children, 5 years
program_terms.location: 'Resident Permit', p. 1
program_terms.quote: Residence Permit – Eden Island Scheme 05 years including endorsement of Spouse and children: SCR 150,000
program_terms.notes: No official minimum property price was found. The ordinary residence permit costs SCR 150,000 for the main applicant plus SCR 75,000 for a spouse and SCR 25,000 per child.

events.title: Investors can naturalise after 2 years (MUR 3 million)
events.description: The Mauritius Citizenship (Amendment) Act 1995 lets the Minister accept 2 years' residence instead of the usual period for a person who has invested at least MUR 3 million.
events.quote: invested in Mauritius a sum of not less than 3,000,000 rupees

events.title: Investor naturalisation threshold raised to USD 500,000
events.description: Act No. 34 of 1999, passed by the National Assembly on 30 Nov 1999, replaces MUR 3 million with USD 500,000 'or such other sum as may be prescribed'.
events.quote: To provide for an increase in the sum to be invested to become eligibles for Mauritian Citizenship

events.title: Occupation permits for investors and residence permits for retirees created
events.description: Sections 9A (occupation permit) and 9B (residence permit for retired non-citizens) are inserted into the Immigration Act by Act 21 of 2006 with effect from 1 Oct 2006.
events.location: annotations to ss. 9A and 9B, PDF p. 10
events.quote: [S. 9B inserted by s. 5 (g) of Act 21 of 2006 w.e.f. 1 October 2006.]

events.title: Residence extended to Property Development and Smart City Scheme buyers (USD 500,000)
events.description: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2015 gives resident status to buyers of property worth at least USD 500,000 under the new PDS and Smart City schemes, and keeps the status of existing IRS and RES owners.
events.quote: the purchase price of which is not less than 500,000 US dollars

events.title: Budget proposes citizenship for USD 1 million and passports for USD 500,000
events.description: The 2018-19 budget speech proposes two EDB schemes: citizenship for a non-refundable USD 1 million contribution to a Mauritius Sovereign Fund (USD 100,000 per family member) and a Mauritian passport for USD 500,000 (USD 50,000 per family member). No implementing law was found in the Finance Acts 2018 to 2026; the proposal appears not to have been carried out, but no official withdrawal was found either.
events.quote: The first scheme will offer foreigners the opportunity to obtain Mauritian citizenship provided they make a non-refundable contribution of USD 1 million to a Mauritius Sovereign Fund

events.title: Property threshold for residence cut to USD 375,000
events.description: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 sets USD 375,000 for residence through all EDB property schemes, cuts the direct permanent-residence investment from USD 500,000 to USD 375,000, lowers the investor permit to USD 50,000 and extends investor and retiree permits from 3 to 10 years.
events.quote: the purchase price of which is not less than 375,000 US dollars

events.title: Family Occupation Permit for USD 250,000 contribution; residence for G+2 apartment buyers
events.description: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2021 creates a 10-year family occupation permit for a USD 250,000 contribution to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund, and residence for buyers of apartments of at least USD 375,000 in buildings of ground plus two floors.
events.quote: Contribution of USD 250,000 or its equivalent in freely convertible foreign currency to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund

events.title: Immigration Act 2022 replaces the 1970 Act
events.description: The Immigration Act 2022 restates the residence routes (property at USD 375,000, retirees, occupation permits, family occupation permit).
events.quote: provided that the purchase price is not less than 375,000 US dollars

events.title: Residence for over-50s buying senior-living property above USD 200,000
events.description: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2023 adds a residence permit for buyers aged over 50 of senior-living property under the PDS priced above USD 200,000.
events.quote: the purchase price exceeds 200,000 US dollars

events.title: Retiree income raised to USD 2,000 a month; permanent residence after 5 years
events.description: The Finance Act 2025 raises the retiree transfer to USD 2,000 a month (USD 24,000 a year), adds a USD 100,000 investor option, and requires 5 years (instead of 3) on a permit before permanent residence. Permits stay valid for 10 years.
events.quote: thereafter a sum of either USD 24,000 annually or USD 2,000 per month

events.title: USD 50 application fee for occupation and retiree permits
events.description: The EDB introduces a non-refundable USD 50 application fee for all occupation permit and retiree residence permit applications.
events.quote: an application fee of USD 50 (non-refundable) is effective as from 01 December 2025

events.title: Golden visa holders investing USD 1 million can get permanent residence; investor permit back to USD 100,000
events.description: In the EDB Act as amended by Act 13 of 2026 (commenced 13 Aug 2026 per the EDB consolidation), golden visa holders who invest USD 1 million within 12 months (not in EDB residential property) qualify for permanent residence; the investor occupation permit requires USD 100,000; the Family Occupation Permit criteria no longer appear.
events.location: First Schedule Parts I and IV
events.quote: has invested an aggregate amount of not less than USD one million

events.title: FATF condemns Seychelles law offering immunity to USD 10 million investors
events.description: The FATF condemns the Seychelles Economic Development Act 1995, which allowed concessions including immunity from prosecution and asset forfeiture for investors of at least USD 10 million; FinCEN tells US banks to scrutinise Seychelles transactions (March 1996).
events.quote: Among the concessions specifically permitted under the law are immunity from criminal prosecution and from forfeiture of assets.

events.title: Economic Development Act repealed; FinCEN withdraws advisory
events.description: FinCEN withdraws its 1996 advisory because Seychelles has repealed the 1995 Economic Development Act; the FATF had also withdrawn its warning. The repeal date itself is not given.
events.quote: the Republic of Seychelles has repealed the 1995 Economic Development Act (EDA)

events.title: Permanent residence and citizenship categories for USD 1 million investors
events.description: Amendments to the Citizenship Act and Immigration Decree (2013) create a permanent resident status, with investors of USD 1 million eligible after 1 year's residence, and citizenship for investors after 11 years' aggregate residence.
events.quote: The Amendments to the Citizenship Act and the Immigration Decree 2013 will introduce the category of the 'Permanent Resident'

events.title: Sierra Leone resumes ordinary naturalisation (8 years' residence)
events.description: The Sierra Leone Immigration Department resumes naturalisation from 1 Oct 2024; applicants must show 8 years' residence. The Citizenship Act 1973 as summarised by the Department has no investment route.
events.quote: IT WOULD RESUME THE NATURALISATION PROCESS WITH EFFECT FROM 1ST OCTOBER, 2024

events.title: GO-FOR-GOLD residency programme launched (reported)
events.description: A press release attributed to the Sierra Leone Immigration Department says a GO-FOR-GOLD 'investment-based residency' programme was launched in December 2024. Its terms (permanent residency through gold purchases and programme fees) come only from promoters; no regulation was found.
events.quote: The launch of the GO-FOR-GOLD residency program in December 2024, promoting investment-based residency opportunities.

events.title: Sierra Leone announces naturalisation for investors (no legal basis published)
events.description: A press release in the name of the Immigration Department announces 'new arrangements' for naturalising high-net-worth investors and people of Sierra Leonean heritage. It gives no amounts and no legal basis. Media reported USD 140,000 (citizenship in 90 days) and USD 100,000 for people of African ancestry (60 days), plus USD 10,000 per dependant. The Citizenship Act requires 8 or 15 years' residence for naturalisation, and no amending act or regulation was found. Recorded as a claim, not as a programme.
events.quote: announces today groundbreaking measures aimed at facilitating the naturalization of qualifying high-net-worth foreign national investors

events.title: Reported prices: USD 140,000 fast-track, USD 100,000 heritage route
events.description: The Sierra Leone Telegraph reports a USD 140,000 'Fast-Track Naturalization' (90 days) and a USD 100,000 'Heritage Naturalization' (60 days) under GO-FOR-GOLD, quoting the Chief Immigration Officer; no official price schedule was found.
events.quote: This groundbreaking initiative provides an efficient alternative to the traditional naturalization process, which typically requires eight years of residence.

events.title: Promoters claim 13 families naturalised under presidential prerogative; regulation pending
events.description: A GO-FOR-GOLD programme update says 13 families were naturalised in a six-month pilot under s. 27A of the Citizenship Act 1973 (the President's power to register anyone as a citizen), that a Citizenship Act amendment and a 'Citizenship (Special Naturalization) Regulation 2025' are pending, and lists fees (main applicant USD 140,000; dependants USD 10,000-20,000; business partner USD 30,000 or USD 85,000, inconsistently). None of this was found in an official publication; s. 27A itself was not read.
events.quote: pending the adoption of forthcoming amendments to the Citizenship Act and the promulgation of the Citizenship (Special Naturalization) Regulation 2025

events.title: Botswana signs MoU with Arton Capital to design a citizenship-by-investment programme (reported)
events.description: The Government of Botswana and Arton Capital announce an exclusive MoU, at the UN General Assembly in New York, to design and launch a citizenship-by-investment programme; no amounts or launch date given.
events.quote: Arton Capital's official press release did not provide any details on investment amounts

events.title: Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2025 with investor citizenship presented to Parliament
events.description: The Minister of Labour and Home Affairs presents the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2025, introducing multiple citizenship and citizenship by investment; the amount would be set later. Investor citizens would not vote, hold public office or receive state land. Whether the Bill was passed was not established.
events.quote: The government has brought before Parliament a bill to introduce citizenship by investment programme

events.title: Nigerian citizenship-by-investment bill passes second reading (reported)
events.description: TechCabal reports that a bill for a new citizenship class for investors in agriculture, ICT and renewable energy passed second reading in the House of Representatives; it would need a constitutional amendment ratified by 24 state assemblies. The bill text was not found.
events.quote: passed its second reading

programs.name: Mauritius residence permit through property acquisition (Integrated Resort Scheme, Real Estate Scheme, Invest Hotel Scheme, Property Development Scheme, Smart City Scheme, G+2 apartments)
programs.notes: Buying qualifying residential property gives the buyer, spouse and dependants a residence permit for as long as the property is held, and the right to work or invest without an occupation permit. Threshold USD 375,000 since the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 (earlier USD 500,000 for RES, PDS and Smart City Scheme; IRS ownership gave residence with no price set in the Act as consolidated to 2009). Senior-living PDS property above USD 200,000 for buyers over 50 since 2023. Approved by the Economic Development Board; now Immigration Act 2022 s. 8. Start date not established: s. 5 of the Immigration Act was amended in 2002, 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009. A path to permanent residence (20 years) exists only for other permit categories; citizenship by naturalisation normally needs 5 of 7 years' residence plus 12 months (Citizenship Act s. 9). EDB published 286 residential acquisition authorisations in FY2020/21; no count of residence permits issued under the schemes was found.

programs.name: Mauritius Occupation Permit for investors, and permanent residence for investors
programs.notes: Combined work and residence permit for a non-citizen investing in a Mauritian business (Immigration Act 1970 s. 9A from 1 Oct 2006; now Immigration Act 2022 s. 12; criteria in the First Schedule to the EDB Act). Minimum USD 100,000 before 2020, USD 50,000 from 2020, both USD 50,000 and USD 100,000 options from Aug 2025, USD 100,000 only from Aug 2026, with turnover targets. Valid 10 years since 2020 (3 years before). Permanent residence (20 years) after 5 years (3 before Aug 2025) with turnover of MUR 15 million a year; a direct permanent-residence route for an investment of USD 500,000, cut to USD 375,000 in 2020, was dropped in 2025; from Aug 2026 golden visa holders investing USD 1 million qualify. EDB reported 918 active investor occupation permits on 30 June 2021.

programs.name: Mauritius Residence Permit for retired non-citizens
programs.notes: Residence for non-citizens aged 50 or over who transfer income to Mauritius (USD 2,500 a month in 2017; USD 1,500 a month or USD 18,000 a year by 2020; USD 2,000 a month or USD 24,000 a year from Aug 2025). Not an investment route, but holders may invest in businesses without working in them. Valid 10 years since 2020 (3 before). Permanent residence after 5 years with USD 200,000 transferred (from 2025). Immigration Act 1970 s. 9B (from 1 Oct 2006), now Immigration Act 2022 s. 10. EDB reported 758 active retiree permits on 30 June 2021.

programs.name: Mauritius Family Occupation Permit (USD 250,000 contribution to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund)
programs.notes: A 10-year residence and work permit for an applicant, spouse, dependants and household staff in return for a non-refundable USD 250,000 contribution to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund (Immigration Act s. 9CA, inserted by the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2021; Immigration Act 2022 s. 14). The criteria were restated in the Finance Act 2025 but are absent from the EDB Act First Schedule as consolidated to Act 13 of 2026, so the current status is unclear. No figures on permits issued or money raised were found.

programs.name: Mauritius naturalisation with reduced residence for investors (Mauritius Citizenship Act s. 9(3))
programs.notes: Not a citizenship-by-investment programme with a price: the Minister may, at discretion, accept 2 years' continuous residence instead of the normal requirement (12 months immediately before plus 5 of the previous 7 years) for a person who has invested at least MUR 3 million (1995) or USD 500,000 'or such other sum as may be prescribed' (1999). The 1995 Act replaced an earlier version of s. 9(3) whose terms were not read. Applicants had to renounce other nationalities (s. 9(4) in the 2003 consolidation). A proposed USD 1 million citizenship scheme in the 2018-19 budget was not legislated. Current text and any use figures were not found.

programs.name: Seychelles Permanent Residence Permit for investors
programs.notes: Permanent residence for a non-Seychellois who has invested the equivalent of at least USD 1 million in a Seychelles business and has lived there legally for 1 year, or has 5 years' business association with Seychelles. Holders can work without a Gainful Occupation Permit and pay 50% of the sanction fee for buying property. Introduced by 2013 amendments to the Citizenship Act and Immigration Decree (texts not obtained; 'launched' is the month of the Department's guide). Permit fee SCR 150,000. Citizenship for investors needs 11 years' aggregate residence (see syc-investor-citizenship). No counts found.

programs.name: Seychelles citizenship under special circumstances for investors (Citizenship Act s. 5(2), 5A-5C)
programs.notes: Not a citizenship-by-investment programme: requires an investment of at least USD 1 million in a Seychelles business plus 11 years' aggregate residence, a citizenship exam (80% in a national language), sponsors and public notices. Fee SCR 350,000 (2020 list). No counts found.

programs.name: Seychelles Residence Permit - Eden Island Scheme
programs.notes: A residence permit category for buyers of property in the Eden Island development, listed in the Immigration Department's fee schedule (SCR 150,000 for 5 years including spouse and children). No official minimum price, legal basis or start date was found; industry sources cite USD 500,000 for property-linked residence permits generally, which was not confirmed officially. The ordinary residence permit is discretionary (family connection or 'special contribution' to Seychelles) and does not allow work.

new_indicators.name: Valid permanent residence permits (stock)
new_indicators.definition: Number of people holding a valid permanent residence permit on a date, as reported by the source, for the categories the source covers (which may include non-investor categories such as professionals or retirees)
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by research:africa-indian-ocean for Mauritius (EDB annual report).

gaps: Mauritius: no official count of residence permits issued under the property schemes (IRS/RES/PDS/IHS/Smart City/G+2) was found; the EDB 'General indicators' real-estate report on residency.mu is behind a form and was not obtained. EDB annual reports for 2018/19 and 2019/20 were found in the Wayback Machine but the copies are truncated (1 MB); 2021/22 onward were not found.

Mauritius: the start date of property-based residence (IRS, around 2002) and of the USD 500,000 RES and direct permanent-residence thresholds were not established from a primary text; the 2002 Finance Act and Investment Promotion (Real Estate Development Scheme) Regulations were not read.

Mauritius: Act 13 of 2026 (golden visa, investor permit at USD 100,000 only, removal of Family Occupation Permit criteria) was not obtained; changes are taken from the EDB's consolidated EDB Act. The golden visa's own eligibility criteria were not found.

Mauritius: the current text of Citizenship Act s. 9(3) was not obtained; the 2003 PMO consolidation reads '5,000 US dollars', which conflicts with the 1999 amending Act (USD 500,000). No figures on naturalisations of investors were found.

Mauritius: no official record was found of the 2018-19 budget's citizenship (USD 1 million) and passport (USD 500,000) proposals being withdrawn; they were simply never legislated in the Finance Acts 2018-2026.

Mauritius: an industry claim that the Finance Act 2025 repealed the USD 500,000 'outside-scheme' property route for residents and cut permit validity to 5 years was not confirmed: the Finance Act 2025 text keeps 10-year permits, and its Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act amendment is a one-word change.
Mauritius: Bank of Mauritius FDI-in-real-estate series and Statistics Mauritius permit data were not obtained (BoM page did not load without JavaScript).

Seychelles: the 2013 amendments to the Citizenship Act and Immigration Decree were not obtained, nor any legal basis or price for the Eden Island residence permit. A reported lifting of a moratorium on property sales to foreigners in January 2025 ('Designated Areas') and a 0.5% property tax for non-citizens from 2026 come only from an industry blog and were not checked. No permit counts found.

Sierra Leone: the Citizenship Act 1973 text (to check s. 27A, the presidential power cited by promoters) could not be downloaded (Refworld blocked); no Citizenship (Amendment) Act or 'Citizenship (Special Naturalization) Regulation 2025' was found on SierraLII or the Immigration Department's current site, which does not mention GO-FOR-GOLD. The 2017 amendment act was not read.

Botswana: whether the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2025 was passed, and any regulations or price (industry reports say USD 75,000-90,000), were not established; the session's web-search budget ran out before this could be checked.
Nigeria: the citizenship-by-investment bill (second reading reported March 2025) was not found on the National Assembly site.

Not covered here: Cabo Verde (assigned to the pacific-gaps brief); Egypt and São Tomé (already in the dataset). No other African investor citizenship or residence programme with an official basis was found in the time available; a broad French/Portuguese search for other countries (e.g. Morocco, Tunisia, Rwanda, Namibia, Guinea-Bissau) could not be run because the web-search budget was exhausted.
